key_insight: The paper introduces two Lean 4 benchmarks to measure how well AI agents can generate machine-checkable proofs in quantum algorithms and quantum information, showing that verified libraries significantly improve performance.
engineering_relevance: These benchmarks provide a reproducible testbed for building more reliable theorem-proving agents for quantum science, where formal correctness matters for future quantum software and research automation.
method: Created Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench (36 tasks) and Lean-QIT-Bench (40 tasks) covering theorem completion in quantum algorithms and quantum information.
Evaluated four models under two settings: task-only baseline and library-augmented deduction (LAD) with access to a verified domain library.
Used deterministic proof checking plus targeted semantic review, with difficulty weights assigned before model execution.
evidence_signal: Across eight model-benchmark comparisons, LAD improved both score and completion rate, with top difficulty-weighted scores of 60.4/100 and 59.6/100 on the two benchmarks.
watch_item: Results depend on a fixed Lean environment and benchmark-specific task distribution, so generalization to broader quantum theorem proving or different formal systems may be limited.
paper_title: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
